0065 SLICE TWO UNIT U6c8: see the unit text below.

TRIAGE DIRECTIVE (operator ruling 2026-10-03): this is an IMPLEMENTATION CHORE. Its specification and design are settled and accepted: openspec/changes/decision-0065-capabilities-slice-two/ (merged as 7f0aa4ad, council-cleared in run build-decision-0065-slice-two-co-50ef1e34) and decision 0077 (accepted). Do not re-specify or re-design: classify it `chore` so it goes straight to implement. It is still reviewed by the full engine council. If the settled design cannot be implemented as written, the implement seat reports blocked; triage does not reopen the design.

BUILD DECISION 0065, SLICE TWO — UNIT U6c8, one narrow visit, ONE pull request. Branch s2/U6c8, cut from main at 6bd45268. Recipe claude-flash-dsh-adv.

READ FIRST: design.md's "Slice two units" preamble and your unit (below, verbatim), the tasks your unit closes in tasks.md, the spec deltas it names, operator-ruling-2026-10-03.md, decision 0077 and decision 0065. Units before yours in your row's Dependencies have landed on main.

THE PREAMBLE, verbatim:
## Slice two units

One row is one PR, from main, signed and through the merge queue after the
operator rules. Follow this order. Dependencies are semantic prerequisites,
not simply the preceding row; the independence of U1–U4 is explicit in D9.
No row through U9a lifts the MCP compile fence. U9b is the sole enabling PR.
The lettered splits are required by the checked seams: record schema plus
embedded copy already consumes two files; multi-server wiring crosses runtime,
protocol and adapter data; storage/folding/inspect crosses CLI, protocol,
runtime and pure view. Minimal ledger writing is deliberately pulled into U6.

`contracts/realms.v<N>.schema.json` denotes one exact future file allocated
as **the next realms version after v7** at U5c, including v7's fields. It is
the only intentionally deferred filename number. Every other production path
below is literal. New paths are proposed modules/schemas, not files created
by this document plan. Constructors/registration are counted in their row.
Future tests extend the named suites; capability_broker already exists under
the consolidated CLI integration binary. New capability_artifacts and runtime
capability_ledger/capability_broker_launch modules are registered through the
existing test-only roots (CLI tests/it.rs and runtime tests/it.rs), not new
undeclared binaries. Tests may use child modules of the owning suites to stay
below 2,000 lines; list every test move in unit evidence.

Each row closes exactly its numbered tasks, including tests/mutations and
gate evidence. Test lists below are the allowed owning suites; every row
also updates this change's tasks and later implementation evidence. Measured
witness/compose pins accompany only rows that change their inputs.

YOUR ROW, verbatim:
| U6c8 | U6c6b, U6c7 | Wire the confined environment handoff; 28.15–28.16 | `crates/brokkr-protocol/src/secret.rs`; `crates/brokkr-cli/src/broker/bootstrap.rs`; `crates/brokkr-cli/src/broker/session.rs`; `crates/brokkr-protocol/src/hands/namespace/entry.rs`; `crates/brokkr-cli/src/cli_args.rs`; `crates/brokkr-protocol/src/broker.rs` |

YOUR UNIT, verbatim:
### U6c8 — Wire the confined environment handoff

Add only the narrow protocol sender/receiver API consumed immediately by session and bootstrap. The sender reads the admitted descriptor after verified readiness, calls bind_environment on a prepared cleared Command and encodes that environment inside secret.rs; receiver validates the same closed frame and builds only the final confined environment. Session consumes the complete preparation/launch operation through the existing command seam; until U6f, `serve` runs the preparation, launch, handoff and exec, then ends the box and refuses with the incomplete-serving cause before any MCP message is exchanged (operator ruling 2026-10-10). No second plaintext accessor, encoding catalogue, shell wrapper, file transport or host env binding. Carry typed read errors from U6c7 and keep secret buffers out of Debug/logging. Require a complete binding frame followed by EOF before actual server exec;
close the sender after its one frame and reject any trailing byte. Close all
unrelated descriptors, keeping only the private typed-failure status pipe marked
close-on-exec until exec. Use that pipe for a typed handoff or exec error, never stderr;
EOF authorizes initialization only, and all startup uncertainty stays failed.
Six production files (operator ruling 2026-10-10): `hands/namespace/entry.rs` carries the private status pipe and the server's standard input and output pipes between the broker and the box; `cli_args.rs` gives the bootstrap its `--status` descriptor; `crates/brokkr-protocol/src/broker.rs` adds `Refusal::Handoff` ("MCP server secret environment could not be delivered") and `Refusal::Exec` ("MCP server could not start inside its box") after `Establishment`. Before exec the bootstrap gives up its controlling terminal, so the box cannot open `/dev/tty` (MB5's terminal isolation, operator ruling 2026-10-10).

Closes tasks 28.15 and 28.16; requirements [MB3](specs/mcp-capability-broker/spec.md), [MB4](specs/mcp-capability-broker/spec.md), [MB5](specs/mcp-capability-broker/spec.md), [SD3](specs/slice-two-delivery/spec.md).
Proof: Single-injector machine proof plus independent host argv/env/pipe-diagnostic leak scans; exact one-frame limits/name equality, EOF/timeout/NUL/duplicate refusals, zero starts on handoff failure, and protected installed server with DOCS_TOKEN and allowed loading names. Fixed HOME/TMPDIR collisions remain zero lookup/start, while missing/invalid store values and delivery failures are accurately post-readiness/post-lookup. Real namespace and bootstrap consumers prove the handoff through `serve`; the MCP compile fence stays unchanged and serving still refuses before any MCP message. A real Linux box cannot open `/dev/tty` once the bootstrap has given up its terminal.
Also bind open-after-frame timeout, truncation, trailing bytes/second frames,
each failure tag, malformed status and bootstrap death at each side of sender completion.
Independently remove the EOF check and status-error propagation. A failed
initialization's own protocol cause is proved where initialization is built
(U6e, U6f), since U6c8 exchanges no MCP message (operator ruling 2026-10-10);
assert the child's exact environment and `/proc/self/fd` with a purpose-built
fixture rather than compensating for a shell's startup changes.

Owning tests: `crates/brokkr-cli/tests/capability_broker.rs`, `crates/brokkr-cli/tests/machine_proof.rs`, `crates/brokkr-protocol/src/secret/tests.rs`.

CONTROLLER'S STATE FOR THIS RUN (the-forge-67, 2026-10-11). This is U6c8's FOURTH run, a REPAIR of ONE finding. It clarifies the commission.

WHY:
- Run 0065-slice-two-unit-u6c8-see-the-0192af28 closed H1: exec_confined now seals every descriptor with close_range before exec, and refuses Exec with zero execs on failure. Its review confirmed that. KEEP it, and all earlier work.
- It then stopped blocked on M1, because no thread can be stopped mid-read. The operator ruled on 2026-10-11 (last addendum in operator-ruling-2026-10-03.md, already in your worktree): A WORKER ENDED BY ITS OWN SESSION'S EXIT IS NOT ABANDONED.
- The worktree arrives with the third run's whole attempt applied UNCOMMITTED on current main: HEAD 9ab1ec16 plus its uncommitted partial M1 work. That partial work is:
  - the store opened O_NONBLOCK through its /proc handle, so a peer-held FIFO or terminal answers at once with its read cause;
  - L2's invariant (fewer prepared entries than bindings refuses Handoff);
  - the reworked readiness tests.
  KEEP it. Keep ALL addenda in your commit. Set quality/file-lines.txt rows to measured counts (readiness/tests.rs is about 709).

FIX M1, by the ruling:
- At the startup deadline or on cancellation, the broker ends the box, settles its cleanup (launcher reaped, pipes closed, admitted identity tree removed) and refuses with Refusal::Handoff AT ONCE, without joining the sender.
- The sender (lookup, bind, serialise, send) runs on a thread that owns its OWN duplicated handles (store, control pipe), so nothing the broker cleans up is borrowed. It ends when `serve` exits on that refusal. Use a detached thread, not a scoped one.
- Prove it with a held regular-file read (the strace delay hold in capability_broker/handoff.rs, about :610-640, or an equivalent seam) at a short deadline, and separately under cancellation:
  - the exact Handoff cause;
  - zero starts;
  - cleanup done;
  - the broker returning within a slice of the deadline or cancellation, not when the held read finishes (the review measured 350 ms after a 40 ms deadline);
  - each with an independent compiling removal (for example, join the sender again and the test must fail).
- In evidence/U6c8.md, record as a host residual a read the kernel cannot release even to a killed process.
- Tick 28.15/28.16 only on observed evidence. The review said they overclaimed.

CARRIED (record, no action): L3 (Launched input/output are temporary and operator-approved), L4 (two frame-reader skeletons; sharing them needs more public API), L6 (U9b's).

BEFORE YOU COMMIT, measure these yourself; CI runs them:
- `cargo crap --path <crate>/src`: new functions at CC 15 or below.
- Every new line, error arm and Display text exercised (CI demands 100%).
- Linux-only code behind cfg(target_os = "linux") with a refusing non-Linux stand-in. CI builds macOS, and CLI-suite expectations go through past_prepare.
- Broker suites under `setsid --wait` where your shell allows. Machine-proof fixtures go OUTSIDE the git worktree (the last chief saw 29 false failures from fixtures nested in it).

GATES:
- `cargo +1.88 check --workspace --all-targets --all-features`
- quality/ratchet.sh api, files, clones, and baselines origin/main (the API growth is ruled)
- CLI `--test it capability_broker::` and machine_proof::, plus the protocol secret tests and the readiness unit tests, with an owner-only TMPDIR where your sandbox allows
- fmt, clippy, `openspec validate --strict`, typos, and `git ls-files -z '*.md' | xargs -0 lychee --offline --include-fragments --no-progress`

A LOW you can't fix inside your files: record it and do NOT report blocked. Commit everything as ONE signed commit.

RE-VOUCH (the-forge-67, 2026-10-11). Run 0065-slice-two-unit-u6c8-see-the-109e0563 delivered U6c8 as PR #625 (M1 fixed by the operator's stuck-read ruling, H1 closed). On CI, three of its real-box tests failed four runs in a row. The controller found the cause with two diagnostic CI runs (#627, #632), and also added one test-only commit.
- ALREADY IN YOUR WORKTREE (keep it): the broker suite holds at most three sealed fixtures, and so real boxes, at once (capability_broker.rs Slot/BOXES). It ended the load-dependent readiness flakes.
- THE CAUSE YOU MUST FIX (test design, handoff.rs): `hold_terminal` and the TERMINAL tracer run strace -f with `-e trace=/^open -P /dev/tty`. With --seccomp-bpf, strace stops EVERY open*/openat of EVERY traced process, -P filtering only afterwards. The broker's observer walks the whole system set with openat, hundreds of thousands of entries on the hosted runner, so each open becomes a tracer round-trip.
  - Under that the observer crawls: the box isn't up within `at()`'s 20 s, giving "no stage … reached: []" with the observer in tracing stop ('tl' in ps).
  - Or the observer overruns the fixed 30 s startup deadline, which is Identity, "filesystem identity is not protected", in a_server_started_from_a_terminal_cannot_open_it.
  - The controller's host has a smaller system set and more cores, so the tests pass there.
- FIX: never trace a syscall the observer issues in bulk.
  - The two hold tests (a_bootstrap_gone_after_the_sender_completed_certifies_nothing, a_status_pipe_open_after_the_whole_frame_is_the_handoffs_cause_at_the_deadline): hold on the bootstrap's TIOCNOTTY instead, `-e trace=ioctl -P /dev/tty -e inject=ioctl:delay_enter=…`, or another syscall only the bootstrap makes. Make sure the stage predicate still finds the bootstrap held at its terminal.
  - a_server_started_from_a_terminal_cannot_open_it: prove "the bootstrap held the terminal and gave it up, and the server can't open it" without tracing the observer's opens. For example, trace only ioctl, plus the server's own evidence of ENXIO. Or attach the tracer to the box's processes once they exist. Keep the proof exact.
- Audit EVERY traced real-box test (handoff.rs, readiness.rs, observer.rs) for the same trap. trace=execve and trace=read on one path are rare enough; anything matching open*/stat* across the tree is not.
- You CANNOT run real-box tests in your box (they skip). The controller runs them on the host, constrained to 2 CPUs to match the runner, before the PR's CI. So write the change carefully, and say in evidence/U6c8.md exactly which tests changed and why.
- Don't change production code unless a test proves it wrong. Fix only what's wrong. Commit as ONE signed commit.

STANDING RULINGS. Decision 0065's hold: off by default, no grandfathering; realm-only grants; tools are an abstraction, dialects the concrete; refuse, never reconcile (slice one's operator ruling of 2026-09-23). The MCP compile fence stays in place until U9b. Hosts are Linux and macOS only (decision 0063). Main's code-health rules bind: no `unsafe` in brokkr-runtime; `#[expect(.., reason)]`, never `#[allow]`; clippy's too_many_lines, excessive_nesting and struct_excessive_bools are denied, so split, and only if splitting would widen your unit carry `reason = "baseline 2026-09-29, decision 0065 slice one merged with main; split after #319"`; when a count moves, re-measure quality/'s file-lines, too-many-lines and suppressions (the steps quality/measure.sh uses), witness pins with `BROKKR_BLESS=1 cargo test -p brokkr-runtime --test witness_digests` (or, once #423's single test binary is on your base — crates/brokkr-runtime/tests/it.rs exists — `BROKKR_BLESS=1 cargo test -p brokkr-runtime --test it witness_digests::`), and budgets with scripts/measure-budgets.sh. Where a crate has tests/it.rs, a NEW tests/*.rs file must be registered as `mod <file>;` in that crate's tests/it.rs (layering::test_targets refuses an unregistered one), unless it sets HOME, cwd, env or a global allocator, in which case it is its own [[test]] in Cargo.toml with the reason written there; and `--test <file>` filters become `--test it <file>::` (capability_launch stays its own binary).

RULES. Touch at most the production files your row names; if the real scope exceeds them, STOP and report `oversized` with the split. One exception, the operator's standing rule of 2026-10-09 (operator-ruling-2026-10-03.md): beside a production file in your row that sits at its 800-line ceiling, or is frozen at its quality/file-lines.txt baseline above it, you may add NEW private child modules, declared from that file, in its own module tree and consumed in this unit, without stopping. The same holds beside a row file that your own change would push past 800 lines (extended 2026-10-11). You may move existing code out of the full file into such a child to make room, preferring the code your change touches. Name each new file in your evidence and commit, and set its quality/file-lines.txt row. You may also add a name to an EXISTING re-export in the parent module that declares one of your row's files, where the parent's line count does not change (extended 2026-10-10). Files in any other module tree still mean `oversized`; any public API growth still needs the operator's ruling at PR time (record it, do not stop). Test files are NOT bounded by the row (controller's standing clarification, 2026-10-05): a test anywhere that pins behaviour your unit changes, a validator or fixture swap in another suite, or a new child test module beside an owning suite that sits over its line ceiling is part of your unit — size-neutral wherever a file sits at its quality/file-lines.txt baseline. A LOW finding you cannot fix inside your row's production files: record it in your result and do NOT report blocked for it. Tests assert exact reasons and values, never is_err(); every new test is bound by a compiling mutation that makes it fail, then restored, recorded (test, assertion) in evidence.md. Tick a task in tasks.md only on observed evidence; record results in a NEW file of your own, openspec/changes/decision-0065-capabilities-slice-two/evidence/U6c8.md (two lanes deliver units at once, and every unit appending to evidence.md made each pair of pull requests conflict), and do not edit evidence.md itself; write it in prose or a table — never as a bullet list of the standard gate lines (`cargo fmt ...: clean`, `cargo clippy ...: clean`), which earlier evidence files already hold word for word, so the data clone gate refuses it; never edit the tasks.md preamble. Fixtures build on a canonicalised temporary root; no test reads .forge/ or needs an installed provider. Frozen contracts, policy/phase-machine.json, fixtures/, reference/ and extensions/ do not move unless your unit names them. Sign every commit (`git commit -S`; main requires signatures). HEADLESS SEAT: your session ends the moment you end a turn — never run a command in the background, never use Monitor or ScheduleWakeup, run every command in the foreground under the tool's 10-minute limit (suites crate by crate with `timeout 590`, split by --lib/--test if longer), and write your result file before you finish. GATES: cargo fmt --all -- --check; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings; the suite of each crate you touched; openspec validate --all --strict; typos --hidden; git diff --check; quality/ratchet.sh files and clones. CI also builds and tests on macOS, which this host cannot: Linux-only code (namespaces, mountinfo, /proc, device numbers, Linux-only syscalls) goes behind `#[cfg(target_os = "linux")]` with a non-Linux stand-in that refuses, as broker/session.rs does, and any libc or rustix type you use must be the same type on both (rustix's Dev is u64 on Linux and i32 on macOS; U6c6a's first PR failed to compile there). Keep the session small; commit when the unit is done; never push.

house.unsupported: OpenSpec ships no constitution; the realm house is authoritative

instructions.analyze:
# OpenSpec analyze

Judge duplication, ambiguity, underspecification, house alignment, coverage gaps, and inconsistency across proposal, deltas, design and tasks. Treat the realm house as the constitution. Return each finding with severity and its earliest owning artifact; zero findings is consistent.
instructions.clarify:
# OpenSpec clarify

Judge underspecified areas, unquantified language, missing decisions, capability/delta mismatches, and requirements without adequate scenarios. Return every ambiguity with the evidence needed to settle it; zero findings is clear.
instructions.design:
# OpenSpec design

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/design.md`. Record context, goals and non-goals, decisions with alternatives, risks, migration, and open questions. On return, revise the design and dependent artifacts so no finding is merely acknowledged.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.
instructions.implement:
# OpenSpec tasks

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/tasks.md` as numbered groups of checkboxes. Name the requirement served by every task. On return, repair the breakdown and its requirement coverage before implementation resumes.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.

Change location: `openspec/changes/{change}`. Archive operation: ["openspec","archive","{change}","--yes"].

# OpenSpec archive

Folding a change is the last task: run the archive operation named above,
which moves the change directory under `openspec/changes/archive/` and
folds its deltas into `openspec/specs/`. Folding also records which change
wrote which capability, so every capability the change touched carries a
`## Provenance` list.

After the archive operation, open each capability's
`openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md` that the change touched and append
exactly one line under a `## Provenance` heading held at the end of the
file:

`- \`<archived-directory-name>\` — folded <YYYY-MM-DD>`

`<archived-directory-name>` is the directory the archive operation
created under `openspec/changes/archive/`; `<YYYY-MM-DD>` is the day it
was folded. Append only: never rewrite, reorder or remove an existing
provenance line, because standing truth accumulates and is not edited into
a different meaning. The line is a pointer, not a summary — it names the
change and nothing else, and the why stays in the change directory.
instructions.review:
# OpenSpec specify

Create or adopt `openspec/changes/<change>/proposal.md`, then write the capability deltas under `specs/`. house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, and `reference/` (its schemas included) are
read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `recipes/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

The supported hosts are Linux and macOS (decision 0063); WSL2 is Linux. Write
no Windows-conditional code, test or evidence.

## Architecture

Decision 0071 rules how code here is shaped. Build to it, and cite its ruling
numbers in what you judge. Where a gate named below holds a rule, the gate is
the authority, and a finding it would catch is the gate's.

- **Pure core (ruling 1).** `brokkr-core` and `brokkr-view` do no I/O and read
  no clock, environment or randomness. They run no process. Pass `now`, paths
  and environment in as arguments. Effects live in the crates above core and
  view, and are journaled.
- **Enums and data, not traits (ruling 2).** A closed set is an enum matched
  exhaustively, with no wildcard arm that decides behaviour. Anything an
  operator extends is data under `adapters/`, `agents/`, `recipes/` or
  `realms.json`, validated and digested. Add a trait only for a seam whose
  contract spans several operations that must stay consistent with one
  another, reached across a process or service boundary, and name that seam
  in its doc comment. `ProducerTransport` is the one such trait today. A test
  double alone does not make a seam: a single substitutable function is a
  closure seam (`*_with`, `*_in`), which is how the house inverts a
  dependency otherwise.
- **Typed at the edge (ruling 3).** Parse wire, file and harness data once
  into a type, with `serde` and `deny_unknown_fields` where the contract is
  closed. `serde_json::Value` never goes past the edge, into state, or back
  out by string key. Never put `format!("{:?}")` in anything digested or
  journaled. A doubly-optional field or a string vocabulary is a missing enum.
- **Small functions (ruling 4).** New and changed functions stay within 100
  lines, nesting depth 5 and 7 parameters. Cyclomatic complexity follows
  the operator's 2026-09-26 ruling: a function may reach the higher of 15
  and its baseline, so a new function stays within 15, an existing one may
  change freely up to 15, and one already over 15 may only shrink.
  Production files stay within 800 lines and test files within 2,000, and a
  file already over may not grow. Add no new `jscpd` clone in production
  code, test code or data. `quality/` holds the measured baseline. Today's
  offenders carry `#[allow(clippy::…)]`, and #337 converts them to
  `#[expect(clippy::…, reason = "…")]`. Add a suppression only by a ruling,
  and remove it when you fix the function. A new suppression is
  `#[expect(…, reason)]`, never `#[allow]`.
- **Once (ruling 5).** Every fact has one home. A repeated vocabulary, skeleton
  or helper becomes one function or one table. An agent is defined once under
  `agents/`, and seats hire it by reference. A recipe that differs from another
  by a model, a seat or an entry is an `extends` overlay, never a copy. The
  agent library does not yet accept `extends`, and #360 builds it. Until then,
  a variation of an agent lives at the seat that hires it, overridden in a
  recipe overlay. It is never a second agent file that restates the first. A
  copy that must exist, such as a script a bundle pins, is held to its source
  by a test.
- **Nothing unused (ruling 6).** Add no alias, agent, contract version, flag or
  `pub` item without a consumer, and prefer `pub(crate)`. A deprecation names
  the release that removes it.
- **One derivation (ruling 7).** A fact shown on two surfaces is derived once
  in `brokkr-view`. The CLI, the TUI and `ui.html` only paint it. The engine
  never admits anything by a display-crate function.
- **Typed errors (ruling 8).** Return a `thiserror` enum whose `Display` keeps
  the operator's text. Tests match variants and pin each module's text once.
  Add no new `Result<_, String>`.
- **Tests that bind (ruling 9).** Assert exact values or variants, never
  `is_err()` alone. Show that every new test binds: a compiling mutation that
  removes the behaviour must make it fail. Restore the behaviour and record
  the failing test. Share fixtures through builders. Never change the process
  environment without a guard that restores it on unwind. A production guard
  left out because the exact-coverage gate would count it unreachable carries
  a removal-control test for the invariant that makes it unreachable, and the
  comment explaining the omission names that test.
- **The house's patterns (ruling 10).**
  - A harness is a module behind `AdapterKind`. This is the target form;
    today all five kinds share one module, and #347 and #348 build the
    split.
  - A CLI verb is a `Cmd` variant plus a handler.
  - A long parameter list becomes a parameter object.
  - Argv and mount tables are built with a builder.
  - Observing the world is split from deciding on it.
  - Never use a trait-object registry for a closed set.

Judges rate a finding against these rulings by this table, and cite the ruling
number:

- **info:** something a house gate would catch. The gate's verdict is the
  authority.
- **low:** a new or changed function over a ceiling, a rule written a second
  time, an item added without a consumer, or a `Value` carried past its edge
  within one module.
- **medium:** an untyped vocabulary that crosses crates, recipe or agent data
  copied instead of extended, a fact derived a second time on another surface,
  an error matched by its text, or a new test that cannot fail.
- **high or above:** any violation that hides a fail-open path or weakens a
  refusal. It is carried as a security finding.

A principle the implementer bent knowingly, and named with its reason in
`notes`, is still rated, and the judge carries that reason with the finding.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.

```json
{
  "repository": "feedback-loop-ai/brokkr",
  "default_branch": "main",
  "tag_format": "v{version}",
  "version_files": ["Cargo.toml", "Cargo.lock"],
  "version_update": "Bump the workspace package and six path-dependency versions together. Run cargo update --workspace --offline without upgrading registry dependencies. Measure and update the witness and compose manifest digests because the engine version participates in their identity.",
  "release_notes": "docs/releases/v{version}.md",
  "handoff_directory": "docs/releases/v{version}",
  "scratch_directory": ".forge/release",
  "documentation": ["README.md", "ARCHITECTURE.md", "CONTRIBUTING.md", "docs/guides/", "packaging/README.md"],
  "validation": [
    {"name": "format", "command": "cargo fmt --all -- --check"},
    {"name": "clippy", "command": "cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings"},
    {"name": "tests", "command": "cargo test --workspace --all-features --locked"},
    {"name": "self bundle", "command": "cargo run --locked -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle recipes/self"},
    {"name": "verify bundle", "command": "cargo run --locked -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle recipes/verify"},
    {"name": "exact coverage", "instructions": "Run bash scripts/coverage-exact.sh in CI or host validation outside the workspace box before tagging. Boundary tests require creating a namespace, which the box deliberately refuses to nest. Record this check as pending in the preparation handoff until that external result exists; never lower the coverage gate."},
    {"name": "release binary", "command": "cargo build --release --locked -p brokkr-cli"},
    {"name": "remote CI", "instructions": "Before tagging, require all applicable CI jobs on the final candidate commit, including both supported operating systems, MSRV, licenses, audit, packaging and exact coverage."}
  ],
  "organization_profiles": [

  ],

    {"name": "crates.io", "evidence": "All seven workspace crates serve the new version."},

  ],
  "extensions": [
    {"name": "workflow toolchain agreement", "instructions": "Check that CI, release admission and local coverage select the same pinned compiler.", "evidence": "Both workflows and coverage-exact.sh consume rust-nightly-version.txt."},
    {"name": "frozen contracts", "instructions": "Compare contracts, fixtures, policy/phase-machine.json and reference against the previous release; explain additive versions and flag modifications to frozen bytes.", "evidence": "A reviewed diff with migration notes for any new contract versions."}
  ]
```

members.adversarial: Security review of U6c8 at HEAD f1d96582 (whole unit vs main 6bd45268). This run's own delta over the merged prior head is test-only: capability_broker/handoff.rs tracers now select ioctl TIOCNOTTY on /dev/tty and read on the store instead of every open*, plus evidence, tasks and quality rows; no production file changed in the re-vouch. No finding above info and no high or critical, so no security hold. Verified: secrets reach the server only as the one bounded control-pipe frame; Refusal::Name carries StoreError Display text that names the store path, line or binding name and never a value; Intent and Launched Debug carry names only; the receiver's Bindings has no Debug and wraps every value in Secret; frame, received body and final environment CStrings are wiped. Fail-closed holds on every receiver path: oversize length, more than 256 bindings, duplicate, renamed, missing or non-object frames, NUL name or value, trailing byte, second frame, truncation and a stalled/errored read all refuse Refusal::Handoff with the exec count at zero; fixed-name replacement refuses; a failed close_range CLOEXEC seal, empty argv or a non-CString program refuses Refusal::Exec before execve; execve is direct with no PATH search and no shell, so the kernel alone judges a script. The status pipe open at the deadline or on cancellation is Handoff, unknown bytes are Exec, and EOF only lets the broker reach serve's unconditional Refusal::ServingIncomplete refusal after the box is killed and reaped, before any MCP message. The detached sender owns duplicated CLOEXEC store and control handles, is not joined, and is refused at once per the operator ruling of 2026-10-11; the store is re-read through the admitted handle's /proc magic link (no path swap) with O_NONBLOCK and 0600 re-checked by fstat on the reopened handle. Non-Linux stand-ins all refuse. Audited every traced real-box test: no open* or stat* selector remains in handoff.rs, readiness.rs or observer.rs, so the observer's bulk openat walk is no longer trapped. Info residuals, carried, no action in U6c8: (a) a status-pipe EOF after a bootstrap death following sender completion is indistinguishable from a successful exec; U6c8 certifies nothing on it, but U6e/U6f must not treat EOF as proof the server started. (b) a write already in flight when given_up is set can still complete; its only reader is the intended confined box, which is being ended. (c) best-effort unwiped copies remain: the injector Command's environment and a serde_json reallocation for an over-bound (refused) frame. (d) a read the kernel cannot release even to a killed process leaves serve unable to exit and the sender's duplicates held; that is recorded as a host residual in evidence/U6c8.md.

That ioctl happens in prepare(), after received() has required the whole frame and EOF (secret/handoff.rs:175-179), so the hold stage still means 'after the sender completed'. The bootstrap issues that ioctl only when it holds a terminal, so wrapping both hold tests in script(1) via Handing::at_a_terminal is necessary and correct. at_its_terminal now short-circuits (&&) before it reads /proc/<pid>/fd, and its added /dev/tty-open condition rules out a passing seccomp stop.
